answer: Node2vec typically reveals two main kinds of node groupings in a novel network: communities of nodes that are densely connected to each other, and structural-role groupings of nodes that are not necessarily close in the graph but play similar roles or have similar connection patterns. The first kind reflects local proximity or homophily, meaning nodes in the same group tend to be directly linked or belong to the same neighborhood. The second kind reflects structural equivalence or role similarity, meaning nodes can be grouped together because they occupy similar positions in the network even if they are far apart. In short, one grouping is about who is connected to whom, while the other is about how nodes function in the network.
